en: 4. The Pairs on Elements (Dhātuyamaka) 4.1 The Section on Designations (Paṇṇattivāra) 4.1.2.
The Exposition of the Section on Designations (Paṇṇattivāraniddesa)
4.1.2.1. Chapter on the Purification of Terms 4.1.2.11.
Positive Order Is the eye the eye-element?
The divine eye, the wisdom-eye, and the [physical] eye are not the eye-element (*cakkhudhātu*). The eye-element is both the eye and the eye-element.
Is the eye-element the eye? Yes.
Is the ear the ear-element?
The divine ear is the stream of craving; it is not the ear-element. The ear-element is both the ear and the ear-element.
Is the ear-element the ear? Yes.
Is the nose the nose-element? Yes.
Is the nose element the nose? Yes.
(The tongue is also similar to the nose element.
Is the body the body element?
Excluding the body-element (kāyadhātu), the remainder is the body, but not the body-element. The body-element is both the body and the body-element.
Is the body-element the body? Yes.
Is matter (rūpa) the matter-element (rūpadhātu)?
Excluding the form element (*rūpadhātu*), the remaining form is not the form element. The form element is both form and the form element.
Is the form element form? Yes.
(Sound is similar to the nose.)
Is fragrance the fragrance-element?
The fragrance of virtue, the fragrance of concentration, and the fragrance of wisdom are fragrance, but not the fragrance-element. The fragrance-element is both fragrance and the fragrance-element.
Is the fragrance-element fragrance? Yes.
Is "taste" the same as "the taste-element"?
The taste of meaning, the taste of the Dhamma, and the taste of liberation are tastes, but they are not the taste-element. Is the taste-element both taste and the taste-element?
Yes. Is the taste-element taste? Yes.
(Tangible object is like the nose.
Is eye-consciousness the eye-consciousness-element? Yes.
Is the eye-consciousness-element eye-consciousness? Yes.
Is ear-consciousness … nose-consciousness … tongue-consciousness … body-consciousness … mind [the mind-element]?
With the exception of the mind-element, the remainder is mind, not the mind-element. The mind-element is both mind and the mind-element.
Is the mind-element the mind? Yes.
Is mind-consciousness the mind-consciousness-element? Yes.
Is the mind-consciousness-element mind-consciousness? Yes.
Is the Dhamma the Dhamma-element?
With the exception of the Dhamma-element, all remaining Dhamma is not the Dhamma-element. The Dhamma-element is both Dhamma and the Dhamma-element.
Is the Dhamma-element Dhamma? Yes.
4.1.2.12. Negative (Paccanīka) Is it the case that what is not the eye is also not the eye-element? Yes.
Is it the case that what is not the eye-element is also not the eye? Yes.
The divine eye and the wisdom-eye are not the eye-element, yet they are the eye. Excluding both the eye and the eye-element, the remainder is neither the eye nor the eye-element.
Is it not the ear and not the ear-element? Yes. Is it not the ear-element and not the ear? Yes.
The divine ear is not the ear-element, but it is the ear. Excluding both the ear and the ear-element, the remainder is neither the ear nor the ear-element.
Is it not the nose and not the nose-element? Yes.
Is it not the nose-element and not the nose? Yes.
The tongue is not...
[Abbreviated; both are affirmed.
Is it not the case that the body is not the body-element? Affirmed.
Is it not the body-element, yet not the body?

With the exception of the body-element, the remainder is not the body-element, but is the body. With the exception of both the body and the body-element, the remainder is neither the body nor the body-element.
Is it not form, yet not the form-element? Yes, it is so.
Is it not the case that what is not the form element is not form?

With the exception of the form element, the remainder is not the form element, but it is form. With the exception of both form and the form element, the remainder is neither form nor the form element.
Is it not the case that what is not sound... [and so on] ...is not odor and not the odor element? Yes.
Is it not the case that there is neither the odor-element nor odor?

The fragrance of virtue, the fragrance of concentration, and the fragrance of wisdom are not the odor-element, yet they are odors. Excluding both odor and the odor-element, the remainder is neither odor nor odor-element.
Is it not the case that there is neither taste nor the taste-element? Yes, it is so.

Is it not the case that what is not the taste-element is not taste? The flavor of existence (*attharasa*), the flavor of the Dhamma (*dhammarasa*), and the flavor of liberation (*vimuttirasa*) are tastes, but they are not the taste-element. Excluding both taste and the taste-element, the remainder is neither taste nor the taste-element.
Is it not the case that what is not tangible... [and so on] ...is not eye-consciousness and not the eye-consciousness-element? Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that the eye-consciousness-element is not eye-consciousness? Yes.
Is it not the case that ear-consciousness … nose-consciousness … tongue-consciousness … body-consciousness [is not so]?
Yes. Is it not the case that the mind is not the mind-element? Yes.
Is it not the mind-element (manodhātu) and yet not the mind (mano)?

With the exception of the mind-element, the remainder is not the mind-element, but it is the mind. With the exception of both the mind and the mind-element, the remainder is neither the mind nor the mind-element.
Is it not mind-consciousness (manoviññāṇa) and yet not the mind-consciousness-element (manoviññāṇadhātu)? Yes, it is so.
Is it not mind-consciousness-element that is not mind-consciousness? Yes.
Is it not a phenomenon that is not the phenomenon-element? Yes. Is it not the phenomenon-element that is not a phenomenon? Yes.
Excluding the dhamma-element (dhammadhātu), the remainder is dhamma, but not the dhamma-element. Excluding both dhamma and the dhamma-element, the remainder is neither dhamma nor the dhamma-element.
4.1.2.2. Wheel Chapter Based on the Purification of Terms (Padasodhanamūlacakkavāra) 4.1.2.21.
Positive Order (Anuloma)
Is the eye the eye-element?
The divine eye and the wisdom-eye are the eye, but not the eye-element. That which is the eye-element is both the eye and the eye-element.
Are the elements the ear-element?
The ear-element is both an element and the ear-element. The remaining elements are not the ear-element.
Is the eye the eye-element?
The divine eye and the wisdom-eye are the eye, but not the eye-element. The eye-element is both the eye and the eye-element.
Are the elements the nose-element …pe… are the elements the mental-object-element?
The mental-object-element is both an element and the mental-object-element. The remaining elements are elements but not the mental-object-element.
(Just as the presentation in the *Āyatana-yamaka* [Pairs on Bases], so too is the presentation in the *Dhātu-yamaka* [Pairs on Elements]. The wheel should be constructed accordingly.)
4.1.2.22. Negative (Paccanīka) Is it not the eye, and yet not the eye-element? Yes.
Is it not an element, and yet not the ear-element? Yes.
Is it not the eye, and yet not the eye-element? Yes.
Is it not an element, and yet not the nose-element … [and so on] … is it not an element, and yet not the mind-object-element? Yes.
(The wheel should be constructed; all are "yes" for both sides, and likewise for the remainder.)

Is the ear an element? Yes.

4.1.2.32. Negative (Paccanīka):
Is it not the eye, and yet not an element?
Excluding the eye, the remaining elements are not the eye, but they are elements. Excluding both the eye and the element, the remaining things are neither the eye nor elements.
Are those which are neither elements nor the eye-element [neither the ear nor elements]? Yes. Are those which are neither the ear nor elements [neither the eye nor elements]? Yes.
Setting aside the ear... setting aside the nose... setting aside the tongue...

[It is] excluding form …pe… excluding sound … smell … taste … tangible object … excluding eye-consciousness …pe… excluding mind-consciousness …pe….

Is it not the case that it is neither a *dhātu* nor a *dhammadhātu*? Yes, it is.
